meta.task: Ship a small feature end to end, from brief to release
meta.title: Ship a Feature End to End
meta.promptIntro: Ship a small feature end to end, from brief to release. Start from the brief and its acceptance criteria, build the feature in verified slices, and finish by opening the PR and cutting the release with the evidence attached.

nodes.label: Gather the brief & acceptance criteria
nodes.description: Ask what the feature must do, who it is for, and what counts as done. Several rounds of clarification before any code can be written.

nodes.label: Research the libraries & read the docs
nodes.description: Open a dozen tabs of API references, changelogs, and issue threads by hand, then copy the relevant snippets somewhere they can be found again. Half the pages are stale and the version that matters is never the one indexed.

nodes.label: Scaffold the module & wire it up
nodes.description: Create the files, imports, config entries, and boilerplate the codebase already expects for a module of this shape, then hook the new module into the router and the build.

nodes.label: Write the feature, one slice at a time
nodes.description: Implement a slice, run it, read the error, adjust. Repeats until the behaviour matches the brief; every slice re-reads the same surrounding code.

nodes.label: Verify it by hand in the browser
nodes.description: Start the dev server, click through the flow, watch the console, resize the window, and check the states nobody remembers to check. Every fix means walking the whole path again from the top, and a missed console error ships.

nodes.label: Open the PR & cut the release
nodes.description: Write the description, attach the evidence, get the review, merge, and tag. The evidence is screenshots taken by hand during the previous step.

suggestions.name: firecrawl-mcp
suggestions.claim: Reads the live docs for you and answers from the page, so the tab-hoarding round trip disappears.
suggestions.install: claude mcp add firecrawl -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp
suggestions.promptFragment: Use firecrawl-mcp to pull the library docs instead of opening a dozen tabs and copying snippets around by hand. Ask it for the pages that matter as soon as the brief is settled, and work from what it returns. Add it first with `claude mcp add firecrawl -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp`.

replaceWith.label: Pull the docs in-session
replaceWith.description: Ask for the API surface and get the current page back inline, cited, without leaving the session.

suggestions.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
suggestions.claim: Drives the real browser and reads the console itself, so the click-through and the missed error both stop being yours.
suggestions.install: claude mcp add chrome-devtools -- npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
suggestions.promptFragment: Once the feature builds, use chrome-devtools-mcp to verify it: let it drive the real browser through the flow and read the console itself instead of clicking through every state by hand. Treat its clean pass as the gate before the PR opens.

replaceWith.label: Verify in a driven browser
replaceWith.description: The flow is walked, the console is read, and the screenshots are captured in one pass — including the states nobody remembers.

suggestions.name: browser-verify plugin
suggestions.claim: Records the click-through once and replays it on every change, so the walk from the top happens without you.

replaceWith.label: Replay the recorded walk-through
replaceWith.description: The recorded path runs on every change and reports the first state that differs, with the evidence attached.

suggestions.name: scaffold-module skill
suggestions.claim: Writes the boilerplate a module of this shape always needs — but this patch is malformed on purpose: it deletes the step and then wires an edge back into it.

suggestions.name: codebase-conventions skill
suggestions.claim: Writes new modules the way this codebase already wires them, so the separate scaffold-and-hook step folds into the coding loop.
